turns.content: My closest friend from college called last night. His father needs a procedure — real thing, I've known uncle for years — and he asked me for eighty thousand, "just for two months." Here's the thing I didn't say: in 2019 I gave him fifty thousand. Neither of us has mentioned it since. Not once, not him, not me.

Meanwhile I'm eleven months into saving for a flat down payment. And my wife doesn't know about the 2019 money — it was before the wedding and it just... never came up, and now it's a thing I've apparently decided not to tell her, which I hate. If I move eighty thousand she will definitely notice.

I was thinking I'll tell him my money is parked in FDs and mutual funds, all locked in, nothing liquid. It's a small lie and it saves the friendship — he keeps his respect, I keep my savings, nobody has to say the real sentence. Is that wrong? It feels smart and it also feels a bit sick.

The part that actually keeps me up: someday he'll be standing in my flat at the housewarming, hugging me, and some part of me will still be doing 2019's math. I don't want to become that person — the friend with a ledger in his chest. But I also can't keep being the guy whose money is everyone's buffer.
